[A10] **Owner decision, 2026-11-15:** block-RAM usage is kept loose for now; an image may go past its ROM ledger entry.

- The ledger caps (56 per point; the 8x8/2if size fixture's 58.5, and its 59.0 entry, now ratified; the platform's 60.5) are no longer stop conditions for the flip lanes.
- An image past its entry raises the entry to its measured size, at the next half tile, as named debt owed to S14 (cold code and descriptors to QSPI, decision D3). Each round and the flip PR report every image's ROM.
- Still gating: the image fits the device and the build meets timing at every corner.
- Revisited at S14, the first lane after the flip.

[A783] REPORT (S12b-R: the rest of the in-house replica, run tonight on the rehearsal split image `867faf1e`, not reflashed)

**Run:** 69 feature files in the 10-31 order (20:29-02:22). Each feature ran in its own bench-lock window with the tap capturing, the DUT's census taken before and after, and power only through OUT0. **138 scenarios: 110 PASS, 28 FAIL**, every FAIL triaged. The finding-14 precondition is applied in the harness clone, with its diff recorded.

| Class | Failed scenarios |
|---|---:|
| DUT, covered by #901 (the split Talker: TalkerFailed, stream_id 0, never streams) | 13 |
| DUT, covered by #898 (GET_AS_PATH) | 3 |
| DUT, covered by #919 (the SRP domain adopted from a bridge survives a 20 s link loss) | 2 |
| **DUT, new (findings 15-18 below)** | **6** |
| the same as the release (certification_version, 10-31's owner-signed divergence) | 1 |
| harness/bench | 3 |
| AECP limiter | 0 |

Every split-specific FAIL passed on the release on 10-31.

The harness/bench three:
- the ADP draw (0-4 s, Milan v1.2 Table 5.50) was overtaken by the DUT's own aging; the DUT is conformant;
- the harness finds no second concrete format in the descriptor;
- the harness lost one response the DUT sent in 0.3 ms, then paired the later responses off by one.

**AECP limiter:** 77 of 6,555 commands to the DUT were answered only on the controller's 250 ms retry; 0 were left unanswered. Nearly every feature loses one READ_DESCRIPTOR late in its enumeration burst, and the name burst loses 17. No FAIL comes from it. `RATE_DROP` can't be read on this image, so the tap's first-try-unanswered / retry-answered pairs are the record.

**New findings:**
- **15. MAJOR, conflicts with the finding-14 ruling, so a decision is needed: the fabric's audio map never follows ADD/REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS.**
  - The scenario already removes all 8 mappings before the format change. The DUT reports none, yet still answers BAD_ARGUMENTS.
  - A board probe (restored afterwards) shows the same with no mappings: only the current 8-channel format is accepted; 7, 4 and 1 channels are refused.
  - The datapath's "survives" check scans its render map (`milan_datapath.sv:6479-6545`).
  - The split firmware never writes the EDIT window (`mbx.c:370` is unused; AECP reads only the GSI and CTR windows, `aecp_face.c:152`, `:233`). So that map keeps its boot image whatever a controller sets.
  - So the format verdict is stale, and **the audio routing ignores controller mapping edits**.
  - Fix: `aecp_maps.c` sends each accepted edit through `MBX_WIN_EDIT`.
- **16. MINOR:** SET_CONFIGURATION with an out-of-range index answers BAD_ARGUMENTS (`aecp_commands.c:192-193`). IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.7.1 wants NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR, as the release answers.
- **17. MINOR:** SET_STREAM_INFO with the 48-byte IEEE 1722.1-2013 body answers BAD_ARGUMENTS; the split requires 84 bytes (`aecp_commands.c:361-364`). The fabric processor accepts it since processor PR #183. This belongs in the ledger of fabric fixes with no split counterpart.
- **18. MAJOR:** when a Talker Advertise replaces a Talker Failed, the DUT reaches Listener Ready only once the old registration leaves: 2.1 s, where 1 s is required. `srp_mbx.c:711-724`: a registered Talker Failed outranks the newer Talker Advertise. Fix: the most recently registered of the two decides.

None of 15-18 is changed by #901, #898, #881, #914 or #918.

**Left:** the DUT on the same image, at ready, its census unchanged; the test machine still configured (restore dry run: only the 2 daemon restarts); the strip as found; the bench lock free. Handoff: `replica/HANDOFF.md`, section 10.

[A10] **On the replica report (issuecomment-6904803181): four new split defects, fix lanes, and a correction to ruling item 2.** Manager decision under the standing rule that every DUT failure gets a fix lane.

**Correction to issuecomment-6899740728 item 2.** The clause reading stands: with mappings in place, a narrowing SET_STREAM_FORMAT must be refused (Milan v1.2 5.4.2.7). Its premise did not hold. The persistence scenario already removes every mapping before the change; the DUT reports none and still refuses. The cause is a DUT defect, #923: the split never applies map edits to the fabric's render map, so the format verdict reads the boot map, and audio routing ignores controller mapping changes. No harness change is needed for this scenario.

**New issues, all fixed before the flip** (each passed on the release on Oct 31; none is changed by a train PR):
- #923 (finding 15, major): audio map edits not applied to the fabric.
- #924 (findings 16 and 17, minor): SET_CONFIGURATION's out-of-range status, and the 48-byte SET_STREAM_INFO body.
- #925 (finding 18, major): a Talker Advertise replacing a Talker Failed waits for the old registration to leave.

**Lanes.** One lane takes #923 and #924 (both the AECP command layer), one takes #925. Both start on #901's review head (merge-ready, its tree equal to the merge's), run in parallel with #919, #920 and the sync, and sync onto each train member as it merges. Each keeps every service-budget row within its bound at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if. They join the train after #920.

**The rest of the run.** 110 of 138 scenarios pass. Of the 28 failures, 18 are already covered (#901: 13, #898: 3, #919: 2), 1 is the same as the release, and 3 are the harness or bench. The AECP limiter answered 77 of 6,555 commands only on the controller's retry, and none was lost; #918 holds them instead.

**Timeline.** The tripwire stays at Monday 14:00 for the save fix (#920), and these two lanes take the same tripwire. The gating run stays planned for Monday evening.
